steps.name: Greta
steps.text: We've concluded that Dalton's death was an accident.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: The medical team is taking his body back to central Wrankwood by short-haul transport. There they'll report the incident to the police.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Shelly has double-checked all the props just in case. So let's take a little break to pull ourselves together, and we'll resume shooting in the afternoon.

steps.name: Staff A
steps.text: That soon?

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Is there a problem?

steps.name: Staff A
steps.text: Cameras and film can be replaced, but we're talking about a dead man here. We've only just wiped up the blood...

steps.name: Staff B
steps.text: How the hell did he go looking for a prop and end up with a real knife?

steps.name: Staff B
steps.text: Did someone trick that washed-up drunk of an actor into looking for a lost prop himself? Or did someone put it in his hands on purpose?

steps.name: Staff A
steps.text: H-Hey now, let's not get carried away here.

steps.name: Staff A
steps.text: Sure, the old man was a drunk and late to the set all the time, but it's not like he had any enemies in the crew. Why would anyone go that far?

steps.name: Staff A
steps.text: Besides, it's just an ordinary knife. There are plenty of them lying around in the crew kitchen, in the convenience stores, even our own rooms...

steps.name: Staff A
steps.text: Maybe someone just mentioned it in passing to Dalton, and then he...

steps.name: Staff B
steps.text: All I'm saying is that it's suspicious, okay?

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Then why don't you ask Dalton yourself, Miss Detective?

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Look, I know you're all shocked at losing a coworker. I feel the same way. But there's something even more important we should be worrying about—

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: We don't have much time left for the shoot.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: I'm sure you haven't forgotten that this studio plate is kept separate from the nomadic city.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: While it's still controlled by the central command tower, the film crew gets direct authority over certain functions, allowing us to drive it outside of central Wrankwood.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: And once the lease ends, the studio closes down, and the plate returns on its own.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: But more space means more costs. According to the contract, extending the lease will result in an expensive penalty—

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Which will be reflected in all of your paychecks.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: As the producer, it's my job to act in everyone's best interests and ensure the film crew can function.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: I agree.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: So do I, as both the lead actress and investor.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Miss Detective here did remind me, though, that someone must indeed answer for this.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Prop Master?

steps.name: Prop Master
steps.text: Y-Yes, ma'am?

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: It was your responsibility to manage the props, and you've clearly neglected it. Even your intern was on set before you.

steps.name: Prop Master
steps.text: I-I'm sorry, ma'am.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Apologies won't cut it, darling.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: You're fired. I suggest looking for a new job before our plate gets too far from the city... And whatever you're about to say, save it. You're getting off easy and you know it.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: You're in charge of the prop team now, Moira.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: M-Me?

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Or you could leave with your former boss, but I trust you're smarter than that.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: As for you, Steven, it's time to get your act together.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: We both agree that The Death of Lady Dupont lacks a strong ending.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: You were supposed to submit the final script for those scenes last week. The shooting is almost caught up with what's written.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: I have my hands full directing, okay? This crew doesn't exactly inspire confidence, you know...

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: So you still haven't found the inspiration?

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: ...Yeah.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: It's your own original script, darling. Your baby. It deserves the very best ending.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: That's my biggest concern as well.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: In the end, which of the Rockefeller boys kills Lady Dupont? Where? How? What are her last words?

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: The ending will determine the quality of the whole film.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: She needs a good, proper death to kickstart the revival of my career in Wrankwood.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: That's the only reason I've poured my entire fortune into this project.

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: ...God will come find me.

steps.name: Melanie
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Oh, in literary criticism we often say that inspiration is like a god descending upon the author, using him as a vessel to write about death and rebirth, destruction and hope...

steps.name: Steven
steps.text: Anyway, don't worry, I'll finish the story.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Good. Then you're dismissed, so get to work.

steps.name: Shelly
steps.text: Miss Stone! Miss Stone!

steps.name: Shelly
steps.text: I need to talk to you about something! It's important—

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: I know what you want to say, Shelly, but now's not the time.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: I have to go check on Lucian. This is his first film, and his first day on set, and something this serious happens...

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: I can't have him running away on us, now can I?

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: As for whatever you're thinking... you're overthinking it.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: I... I'm in charge of the whole prop team?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Omigosh, congrats, Molly!

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: I mean, it's a shame about Dalton—may he rest in peace—but still, I'm happy for you.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: I've been working here in Wrankwood for way longer than you, but I'm still stuck doing backgrounds, while you just got the chance of a lifetime! Life really is like a box of chocolates, huh!

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: That's because you always put so much of yourself into your work. The art director isn't comfortable letting you handle more.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: But I'm just a girl from the pioneer zone who's good with her hands and came here looking for a job. Can I really do this...?

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: If the producer says you can, you can! She's never wrong about people.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: Your sister will be happy, won't she? You came to Wrankwood because of her, right? You gotta tell her you've been promoted to prop master!

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: I'll call her after we clock out. Miss Stone put her trust in me, so I have to do this right.

steps.name: Tippi
steps.text: That's my girl! You're already sounding the part. I bet in just a few days, you won't even have time to watch horror flicks with me anymore.

steps.name: Moira
steps.text: Tippi!

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: Stop walking in front of me, Shelly!

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: You already checked the storyboard three times and the equipment five times. I swore to the producer that I wouldn't lose another set of cameras. Now can you stop glaring at me like that?

steps.name: Shelly
steps.text: (Whispers) Do you think... it was really...?

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: What was that? Speak up.

steps.name: Shelly
steps.text: Do you think Dalton's death was really just an accident? Doesn't it seem strange to you?

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: Don't know, don't care.

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: I've lost count of how many times I've had to work overtime because that has-been got lost in a beer keg. Good riddance.

steps.name: Shelly
steps.text: He wasn't like that five years ago.

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: No shit, he was at the top of the world, starring in Greta and Steven's next big thing. How could I forget that when we were both there?

steps.name: Shelly
steps.text: That's the weird part!

steps.name: Shelly
steps.text: I saw a lot of familiar names on the staff list during the planning meetings. And when I saw your face, I got this eerie feeling, like—

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: Like we were back five years ago, witnessing that young actress's death again?

steps.name: Shelly
steps.text: Doesn't it all seem a little... similar?

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: How so? One was a fall, the other was a prop mix-up.

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: You're overreacting, Shelly.

steps.name: Shelly
steps.text: I'm telling you, I'm not crazy... Ah, now I remember! Dalton was the one most responsible for the accident!

steps.name: Shelly
steps.text: Judgment has come... Someone came for him...

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: Just stop already! Stop scratching your arm, and stop coming up with this nonsense! I told you: if what happened still bothers you that much, get therapy and stay away from the set.

steps.name: Abner
steps.text: We're just ordinary joes shooting crappy movies for a living. Nobody gives a flip about us. Shelly? Do you hear me, Shelly?

steps.name: Shelly
steps.text: I hear it... I hear it... Something's coming... coming for us...

steps.name: 'Whiteflower'
steps.text: Picture the position and angle of the stab in your mind.

steps.name: 'Whiteflower'
steps.text: Near the bottom-right of the abdomen is a gap between vital organs, rich in blood supply, but not immediately lethal. You can feed off the blood of others, and let it herald the climax that is to come.

steps.name: 'Whiteflower'
steps.text: Or, you can move the point of the knife up and penetrate the thorax.

steps.name: 'Whiteflower'
steps.text: The lungs are fragile and offer no resistance. Your target will drown in both his own blood and your animated monologue.

steps.name: 'Whiteflower'
steps.text: Raise your dagger, boy.

steps.name: 'Whiteflower'
steps.text: Think back to the segments we've rehearsed. You've done well. There's only one step to go.

steps.name: 'Whiteflower'
steps.text: Stab! Let the point of the knife know how it feels to stir the organs and sever blood vessels, and let it listen to the sound of the heart beating!

steps.name: 'Whiteflower'
steps.text: Are you afraid?

steps.name: 'Whiteflower'
steps.text: ...How ordinary.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: He's not afraid. He just doesn't understand.

steps.name: 'Whiteflower'
steps.text: He's still not willing to practice stabbing. He hasn't spoken a single word since he took up the dagger.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Go prepare for tomorrow's performance.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: ...I will instruct him myself.

steps.name: 'Whiteflower'
steps.text: I see... Understood.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Do you find the dagger heavy?

steps.name: Young Lucian
steps.text: ...Yes.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: But its weight does not come from the metal, nor from the ornaments. It comes from your heart. Do you understand?
The boy's hair covers his eyes. He nods in silence.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Whiteflower does not realize that you've learned so quickly. You're waiting for her to provide answers she cannot give you.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Listen to me, child...
The Troupe Leader holds Lucian's little hands in his own. His smile is warm and gentle, but his iron grip permits no refusal.
Lucian can feel his stiff fingers begin to relax.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Forget the techniques that Whiteflower's been trying to teach you. You have no need to imitate any form, or any method of stabbing.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: There is no dagger without blood on it, no crossbow that is not fired. Just hold them.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: They are not props. They will tell you what to desire.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Let them guide you. Do not doubt them, even if they point you towards someone you never expected—a friend, a lover, even yourself...

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Perhaps even me, standing before you now.

steps.name: Young Lucian
steps.text: You... you?

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Have no hesitation. Stab.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Give it a try.

steps.name: Young Lucian
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Try it.

steps.name: Young Lucian
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Try it.

steps.name: Young Lucian
steps.text: Then you, and I...

steps.name: Young Lucian
steps.text: What roles are we playing?

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: If we're forgetting the techniques, then forget the characters and the script as well. They're simply the medium of theater, not theater itself.
Lucian grips the knife. The Troupe Leader lets go of his hand and kneels in front of him, so that their gazes are almost level.

steps.name: Young Lucian
steps.text: But we're too close to each other...

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Are you afraid you'll hurt me?

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: It's alright, child.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Forget even that feeling.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: You will immerse yourself in theater, and touch upon its beauty.
Gazing at the Troupe Leader, Lucian finds himself overcome with doubt. Is this really the first time he has seen the man?
He does not understand what he is saying. He begins to doubt whether the Feline before him even exists at all.
Lucian can feel his own heart throbbing.
The heartbeat never lies. The heartbeat knows the answer.
How should he ask it?
The Troupe Leader smiles, encouraging him wordlessly.
The answer is obvious.
Without hesitation, Lucian thrusts—

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Did you feel it?
Lucian's hands are trembling. He feels them grow weak, almost letting go of the dagger.
The Troupe Leader has not moved an inch, not even a flicker of expression.
Lucian is certain his knife found its mark in the man's body. He heard a sound... felt the pain that should not have belonged to him, a strong, willful pain.
He had been silent since he came to the Troupe. Now, though, the pain makes him want to sing.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: This is your first lesson. All stories leave behind only certain emotions, or...
The Troupe Leader pauses. Lucian casts a questioning glance, and meets those golden eyes.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: A bond so tight that it cannot be broken.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: You're a natural actor. You should study with me.

steps.name: Troupe Leader
steps.text: Think about it, then come and find me... I will never be an obstacle to you, Lucian.
Lucian looks down at his hands.
The blood on his gloves has been washed away, but he remembers the feeling of taking Dalton's knife out of his hands.
Fascination, revelry.
The complex emotions he felt when he was taught to use a dagger for the first time.
Forget complicated assassination techniques. Ignite the ego with intense emotion, until all that is left is two souls tearing at one another.
Let life converge upon the knife of truth and falsehood, and bestow upon the target the perfect ending—
Death.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Come in.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: Lucian.

steps.name: Lucian
steps.text: Madam Stone.

steps.name: Greta
steps.text: You look pale... are you alright?
